results.name: round_target_minus_neighbors
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate for non-example targets ending in 1 or 9; observed above null means people favour round-number targets more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: round_target_minus_neighbors
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets that are multiples of 10 minus yes rate for non-example targets ending in 1 or 9; observed above null means people favour round-number targets more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    rnd = (t % 10 == 0)
    nb = (t % 10 == 1) | (t % 10 == 9)
    v = r[rnd & ~isin].mean() - r[nb & ~isin].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: single_example_near_large_minus_small
results.description: For single-example sets, yes rate on non-example targets within 10 of the example when the example is above 50 minus when it is 50 or below; observed above null means people generalize more broadly around large numbers than the model's Weber width predicts, below means less.
results.code:
# name: single_example_near_large_minus_small
# description: For single-example sets, yes rate on non-example targets within 10 of the example when the example is above 50 minus when it is 50 or below; observed above null means people generalize more broadly around large numbers than the model's Weber width predicts, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)

results.name: shared_digit_far_targets
results.description: Among targets more than 15 from every example, yes rate when the target shares any digit with any example minus when it shares none; observed above null means people use loose digit-feature similarity beyond the model's explicit digit rules.
results.code:
# name: shared_digit_far_targets
# description: Among targets more than 15 from every example, yes rate when the target shares any digit with any example minus when it shares none; observed above null means people use loose digit-feature similarity beyond the model's explicit digit rules.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.replace(",", "", regex=False)
    ts = t.astype(str)
    sh = pd.Series(False, index=df.index)
    for d in "0123456789":
        sh = sh | (ex.str.contains(d, regex=False) & ts.str.contains(d, regex=False))
    far = nd > 15
    v = r[far & sh].mean() - r[far & ~sh].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: prime_minus_odd_nonprime_all_prime_sets
results.description: Among sets of 2+ examples that are all prime, yes rate on prime non-example targets minus yes rate on odd non-prime targets; observed above null means people discriminate primes from merely-odd numbers more sharply than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: prime_minus_odd_nonprime_all_prime_sets
# description: Among sets of 2+ examples that are all prime, yes rate on prime non-example targets minus yes rate on odd non-prime targets; observed above null means people discriminate primes from merely-odd numbers more sharply than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    P = [p for p in range(2, 101) if all(p % a for a in range(2, int(p ** 0.5) + 1))]
    allp = x.isin(P).sum(axis=1).eq(n) & (n >= 2)
    tp = t.isin(P)
    odd = (t % 2 == 1)
    v = r[allp & tp & ~isin].mean() - r[allp & odd & ~tp].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: ap_next_minus_mirror_2ex
results.description: For 2-example sets a,b, yes rate on the next sequence term 2b-a minus on the mirrored term 2a-b (equally far from the nearer example); observed above null means people continue a two-step sequence in its shown direction more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: ap_next_minus_mirror_2ex
# description: For 2-example sets a,b, yes rate on the next sequence term 2b-a minus on the mirrored term 2a-b (equally far from the nearer example); observed above null means people continue a two-step sequence in its shown direction more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    a = x[0]
    b = x[1] if x.shape[1] > 1 else a
    two = (n == 2) & (a != b)
    v = r[two & (t == 2 * b - a)].mean() - r[two & (t == 2 * a - b)].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: adjacent_minus_nearby_targets
results.description: Yes rate on non-example targets exactly 1 from the nearest example minus yes rate on targets 3-5 from the nearest example; observed above null means generalization falls off more steeply right next to the examples than the model predicts, below means flatter.
